business.what: Value hypermarket chain: everyday low cost / everyday low price (EDLC/EDLP) on food, FMCG and general merchandise and apparel. 500 stores, 20.6 mn sq ft at Mar-26 (503 / 20.7 mn at Jun-26); 84 distribution centres and 12 packing centres; first store 2002 in Mumbai.
business.model: Owns most stores (land and building): 68 of 500 stores on long leases at Mar-26, 15 of the 85 stores added in FY26 leased. Pays vendors fast (7.2 payable days) for better buying terms; ~33 days of inventory. Gross margin held at 14-15%; net margin ~5% is the 'North Star'.

dmartReady.note: Consolidated less standalone proxy (Nuvama, Citi); exited 7 cities

q1fy27.colour: Gross margin up ~50 bp y/y (Emkay, JPMorgan); staff cost +30%+ (Jefferies); older large-metro stores flat (Emkay, Goldman Sachs); bills per store -4.4%, average bill +1.5% (Elara); GM&A +19% (Emkay). Board approved a Rs1,000 cr NCD.
q1fy27.src: Q1FY27 presentation (11-Jul-2026); Screener (standalone and consolidated quarterly); Business Today, Upstox and Goodreturns roundups of broker notes, 13-Jul-2026

guidance.storeAdds: Internal benchmark: add ~15% of the store base each year; a few points higher or lower depending on land and approvals (MD & CEO, 28-Jul-2026). 2-3 year pipeline of sites; land to store takes 2-3 years. Open to long leases (NCR) and stores under 40,000 sq ft.
guidance.margins: Gross margin 14-15% and net margin ~5%; savings passed to customers; staff cost built 'ahead of the curve'.
guidance.lfl: Same-store growth for older stores to hover around last year's level (~8%); metro stores near saturation, some loss of small baskets to quick commerce expected to persist.
guidance.gma: General merchandise and apparel to settle at 22-23% of revenue.
guidance.dmartReady: Focus on 11 cities with 6-hour slotted delivery for large baskets; no quick-commerce model; aim to cut losses significantly; no merger with the store business.
guidance.debt: Borrowings may reach ~Rs2,000 cr by Mar-27 (CP plus a Rs1,000 cr NCD) to fund capex; capex 'upwards of Rs4,000 cr' in FY26.

history.event: Avenue Supermarts founded by Radhakishan Damani; first DMart store opened in Mumbai in 2002
IPO priced at Rs299 a share (8-10 Mar 2017), listed 21-Mar-2017
QIP of 2 crore shares at Rs2,049 (Feb-2020), ~Rs4,098 cr raised, taking promoter holding towards the 75% public-float limit
Covid lockdowns: FY21 revenue -3%, like-for-like -13.1%; 22 stores opened, 2 converted into DMart Ready fulfilment centres

Ignatius Navil Noronha completed his tenure as MD & CEO on 31-Jan-2026; Anshul Asawa CEO from 1-Feb-2026 (MD & CEO). 85 stores opened in FY26 (58 in Q4) to reach 500; first commercial paper issued; DMart Ready narrowed to 11 cities; Rs1,000 cr NCD approved (Jul-2026)
